is_anopheles.evidence: The study evaluated Anopheles gambiae and Anopheles coluzzii laboratory strains (Kisumu, Busia, Tiassalé, and Tiefora) as described on pages 2 and 11.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper mentions Vgsc-995S and Vgsc-995F allele frequencies for the colony strains by citing previous literature (refs 21, 22, 23, 24 on page 2), but does not perform new marker genotyping.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No extractable genotype counts, allele counts, or genotyped sample sizes were generated or reported in this study.

african_field_population.evidence: The bioassays were performed exclusively using long-established laboratory insectary strains (Kisumu, Busia, Tiassalé, Tiefora) maintained at LSTM (page 11). No African field populations were collected or tested.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical laboratory study investigating ITN surface chemistry, physical properties, and mosquito behavior.

sub_country_location.evidence: No field mosquito collection locations were surveyed in this study.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: No field collection window for mosquitoes exists for this study.

duplicate_risk.evidence: Not applicable as no field sampling or marker genotyping was performed.

supplement.evidence: No supplementary file is needed because the paper is ineligible due to lack of field mosquito genotyping.

assessment.summary: This study presents a multidisciplinary framework examining the surface chemistry, deltamethrin presentation, and mosquito behavioral responses to PFAS-containing vs PFAS-free PermaNet 2.0 ITNs. Tests were conducted using laboratory colonies (Kisumu, Busia, Tiassalé, and Tiefora). No new field collections or resistance marker genotyping were carried out.
exclusion_reasons: Does not report primary target marker genotyping data.
Does not report extractable genotype data.
Does not test African field populations (uses laboratory colonies only).
